dedupe_keys.name: long term monitoring of sediment accumulation in gully pots using thermal analysis

description: Regueiro-Picallo, Manuel and colleagues publish this resource through the source community. Temperature-based MONTSE devices monitor sediment accumulation in six gully pots across two Zurich catchments. Coverage spans seasonal changes during a long-term field campaign, though exact dates are unspecified. The source reports mean depth-estimation errors below 20 mm against in-situ measurements and accumulation rates varying across sites. This case documents field validation of the related MONTSE model; the original laboratory model and a field monitoring case are distinct resources. A raw time-series deposit is not identified in the abstract. Zenodo supplies the descriptive publication with open access under cc-by-nc-4.0. The publication does not establish public access to an implementation or its separate licence. A limitation is that complete implementation or measurement settings cannot be reconstructed from descriptive metadata alone. Related experimental components and publications retain their distinct roles; separate deposits are not assumed to provide independent observations. The field study supports validation of sediment-depth inference for drainage condition monitoring.
